subject.title: control-ui: expose reply-to metadata to agent sessions and avoid confusing no-output completion notices

question: Should this issue be handled as two coordinated tracks: structured inbound reply metadata plus durable final-fallback delivery semantics, or should maintainers sponsor one combined Control UI/Gateway contract?
rationale: Current main partially addresses the UI affordance and runtime-context carrier, but the remaining behavior crosses Control UI protocol, agent runtime context, and final delivery semantics; automation should not choose that product boundary while an open conflicting PR and a maintainer-labeled fallback issue exist.

options.title: Split Across Existing Tracks
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, review or replace the reply-metadata PR for the structured metadata half, and use the durable final-fallback issue for no-output terminal semantics.

options.title: Sponsor One Combined Contract
options.body: Have an owner define one Control UI/Gateway/session contract that covers both reply metadata and no-output terminal display before implementation resumes.

options.title: Defer Until Fallback Contract Lands
options.body: Pause new Control UI reply work until durable final fallback semantics are settled, accepting that reply metadata remains text-only meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Split Across Existing Tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, review or replace the reply-metadata PR for the structured metadata half, and use the durable final-fallback issue for no-output terminal semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The current blamed and recently maintained lines span both Control UI send handling and agent runtime-context assembly, making this the best available routing candidate from code history.
